 Gujarat Pensioners Dearness Allowance Hike | 443% DA & Arrears Update
 State pensioners under 5th Pay Commission get DA hike: DA raised to 443% from January 1, 2024, with arrears for 2021–2024; full benefit explained
 Gandhinagar 21 hours ago 
 Copy link 
 The Gujarat Government's Finance Department has passed an important resolution to increase the dearness allowance for state pensioners and family pensioners drawing pensions under the Fifth Pay Commission.
 According to the state government's resolution, the dearness allowance rate has been increased to 443% with effect from 1 January 2024. It also provides for the payment of arrears, meaning the difference in dearness relief for various periods from 1 July 2021 to 30 June 2024.
 Government considers raising temporary increase from 381% to 443% 
 How much will pensioners benefit? Understand it with this example 
 The benefit a pensioner will receive depends on their basic pension and the arrears period. For example, if a pensioner's basic pension is ₹10,000, the dearness allowance at the rate of 381% would be ₹38,100, while at the rate of 443% it would be ₹44,300. Accordingly, the difference between the two rates is ₹6,200 per month.
 Earlier, from 1 October 2024, the dearness relief rate was 381%. The new resolution has approved a rate of 443% with effect from 1 January 2024.
 This means that, compared with 381%, the difference is not an increase of 62%, but an additional amount equivalent to 62% of the basic pension.
 These rates apply to the concerned employees covered under the Fifth Pay Commission. It should not be assumed that the 443% rate applies to all government employees and pensioners.
 How much has the dearness relief rate increased? The dearness allowance rate for employees covered under the Fifth Pay Commission has been revised from time to time. See the revised rates in the graphics.
 For which period will the arrears be paid? 
 Details have been provided for the payment of the difference in dearness relief pending since 1 July 2021.
 If a pensioner wants to calculate the arrears for the period from 1 January 2024 to 30 June 2024 (6 months)… 
 Difference percentage = 131% Difference for 1 month = ₹10,000 × 131% = ₹13,100 Total arrears for 6 months = ₹13,100 × 6 = ₹78,600
 According to the Finance Department's recent resolution, 131% represents the arrears percentage for pensioners covered under the Fifth Pay Commission.
 This means that the difference between the dearness allowance previously paid by the government for the period from 1 January 2024 to 30 June 2024 and the revised dearness allowance has been fixed at 131%.
 This amount will be calculated on the old rate of 312% and paid to pensioners as arrears. In simple terms, pensioners will receive an amount equivalent to a 131% difference on their basic pension as arrears for this period.
 Decision also taken to pay outstanding amount 
 According to the Finance Department's resolution, the difference in dearness allowance payable for the previous period-that is, the arrears-will also be paid.
